summary: Backend-only auth/RBAC/audit testing for CareGrid against local FastAPI at 127.0.0.1:8000. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_auth_endpoints.py (22 tests) covering login/me, generic-error contract, missing-fields 400, logout, brute-force 5->429 lockout, inactive-user 403, RBAC on POST /patients + /allocation (no-token=401, Nurse/Coordinator/Administrator=403 'Access Denied', Doctor=success), audit attribution (decision_maker/actor_email/actor_role from token), Override/Defer empty-reason=400, admin user-management CRUD + reset-password + validation (invalid email/duplicate/short password), Doctor calling /users =>403, bcrypt $2b$ hash storage, no password_hash in responses, and prioritization weights (35/25/20/10/10) still sum to 100. Existing regression suites (test_caregrid_v2.py + test_caregrid_v2_new_features.py, 35 tests) all pass with Doctor-token auth. Total: 57/57 passed.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py authenticate() correctly returns generic 'Invalid email or password.' for both unknown-email and wrong-password paths (verified — no user enumeration).
get_current_user re-validates the user row (existence + active) on every request instead of trusting the JWT claim only — safe against stale tokens after deactivation. Good.
Bcrypt hashes verified in SQLite users_auth — all rows start with $2b$. No plaintext leakage in /auth/me or /users responses.
log_audit persists actor_email + actor_role from the token, not from client-supplied fields — audit attribution is trustworthy.
Prioritization weights unchanged (severity 35 / dependency 25 / deterioration 20 / waiting 10 / resource 10) — verified via /priority/calculate hitting exactly 100.0 at max scores.
Minor: /auth/logout is a no-op (stateless JWT) — acceptable per spec but consider a server-side revocation list for defense-in-depth in the future.
Minor: brute-force counter is keyed by email only (not IP+email); an attacker could weaponize lockout to DoS a known user. Non-blocking for MVP.

success_rate.frontend: skipped (Streamlit — main agent covered via AppTest)

test_credentials: Read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md — admin@caregrid.local, doctor1/doctor2/nurse/coordinator@caregrid.local. Passwords used only in test constants sourced from that file.
seed_data_creation: Test-scoped ephemeral data only: one throwaway user via POST /users (deleted from users_auth + login_attempts in finally block); one test patient TESTAU_<hex> via POST /patients (deleted from patients + audit_logs in finally). Nurse was temporarily deactivated then reactivated. login_attempts cleared for all test emails.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Local FastAPI runs on 127.0.0.1:8000 (NOT the preview URL, NOT 8001). SQLite lives at /app/data/caregrid.db. Regression + auth tests live under /app/backend/tests/ and run via `cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/ -v`. Auth is JWT Bearer (12h TTL), tokens obtained via POST /auth/login. To reset brute-force state during ad-hoc testing: `sqlite3 /app/data/caregrid.db 'DELETE FROM login_attempts;'`. Streamlit UI is NOT proxied by the k8s ingress — do not attempt browser testing; use AppTest fixtures instead.
